concepts.title: LLM lettermark
concepts.prompt: Use case: logo-brand. Create a new geometric logo alternative for LLMLean, an open-source project using large language models for Lean theorem proving. The input image is the approved reference for visual style: retain the same dark navy and muted blue palette, flat clean geometry, bold sans-serif wordmark, horizontal emblem-on-left arrangement, and plain white background. Keep the exact text "LLMLean" unchanged and carefully kerned. Change the emblem substantially to explore the requested new idea. Make ONE finished logo, not a contact sheet. Keep the symbol compact and simple enough to identify at 24px, with consistent stroke widths and intentional negative space. No concept labels, tagline, gradients, texture, shadows, 3D, cubes, brains, robots, sparkles, checkmarks, speech bubbles, or rounded-square containers. This should look like a precise, elegant open-source developer tool identity. New emblem direction: explicitly fuse the three letters L L M into one compact geometric monogram. Two navy L-shaped strokes nest together, while a muted blue angular M shape shares a vertical stem with the second L. The M should remain recognizable through its central V-shaped notch; the two L forms should remain recognizable through their right-angle bases. Clever shared strokes, crisp corners, and a balanced silhouette, not three separate typeset letters. Show the language-model initials through the letterforms themselves. Preserve the restraint of the reference.
